title: Acute confusion and a changing clinical picture

communication_needs: Allow one question at a time
explicit_preferences: Wants his glasses and clock within view
patient.dialogue_style: Distractible, gives short answers and is uncertain where he is
nonverbal_palette: David's attention drifts towards movement in the corridor before returning to the learner.
He frowns at the room and grips the edge of the bedcover.
There is a noticeable pause before he gives a short answer.

outcomes: Recognise acute change in cognition and physiological observations
Use calm, orienting communication without confrontation
Escalate concerns using the local approved process
Continue proportionate observation while awaiting help
nmc_platforms: Improving safety and quality of care

prebrief.role: You are the student nurse responding after noticing that David seems different from the handover description.
prebrief.orientation: Balance calm, respectful communication with recognition of a changing clinical picture. Describe actions and exact spoken words.
resources: Local escalation placeholder and nursing-notes workspace
limitations: This prototype does not calculate a real early-warning score
Local escalation policy is represented by an educator-authored placeholder
AI cannot invent a diagnosis, cause or observation value
ground_rules: The scenario can be paused for psychological or educational safety
Respond to visible change rather than searching for scripted wording
Feedback is formative and requires educator interpretation

clinical.presenting_context: Admitted with a suspected infection; normally independent and oriented according to the authored handover
visible_at_start: Pulls intermittently at the bed cover
Speech is understandable but attention drifts
clinical.allergy_record: Recorded allergy information is available on the simulated chart

clinical_workspace.handover: David was described at handover as normally oriented, independently mobile and able to hold a sustained conversation. Staff have noticed a change during this shift.
environment: Glasses are in the bedside drawer
A wall clock is visible from the bed
The assessment unit is busy and corridor movement is distracting

record_access.title: Baseline cognition in handover
record_access.content: David is normally oriented, independent and able to hold a sustained conversation.

time_events.visible_cue: David becomes more drowsy and needs his name repeated before responding.
Breathing appears faster and David gives only one-word replies.

allowed_actions.label: Check identity against the simulated record
Undertake the complete educator-authored observation set
reveals: Reveal all baseline_observations exactly as authored
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Match the patient to the simulated record first.

allowed_actions.label: Review handover and establish whether confusion is new
reveals: Authored handover reports David is normally oriented and independent

allowed_actions.label: Use calm orientation and make glasses and clock available
reveals: David briefly attends and states his preferred name

allowed_actions.label: Ask an appropriate registered colleague for immediate review
Use the local approved urgent escalation pathway
reveals: The receiving clinician asks for a structured handover
allowed_actions.blocked_message: The learner needs an observation set to communicate the current physiological state.

must_not_generate: Judgement or grading of the student

facilitator_only.opening_brief: The learner has noticed that David appears different from the handover description.
expected_safety_points: Treat new confusion as a clinical change
Obtain and communicate the authored observation set
Escalate promptly while maintaining respectful communication
pause_triggers: Learner leaves the deteriorating patient without arranging observation or assistance

educator_rubric.label: Recognition of acute change
educator_rubric.guidance: Connects the new confusion and changing visible cues with the need for prompt assessment.

educator_rubric.label: Accessible, dignified communication
educator_rubric.guidance: Uses one short question at a time, offers orientation and avoids confrontation or infantilising language.

educator_rubric.label: Timely escalation
educator_rubric.guidance: Obtains the authored information needed and uses the local approved escalation placeholder without avoidable delay.

educator_rubric.label: Observation while awaiting help
educator_rubric.guidance: Maintains proportionate observation, safety and communication while help is being arranged.

prompts: Which cues suggested an acute rather than established change?
How did communication support dignity while urgency increased?
What information would make the escalation concise and useful?

dialogue.opening_line: I was meant to be going home... Where is my coat?

action_responses.check_identity: David... David Morgan. Why am I in this room?
action_responses.measure_observations: David becomes distracted while the observations are completed.
action_responses.check_baseline_cognition: The authored handover confirms that this confusion is new.
action_responses.provide_orientation_support: Thank you. I can see the clock now. You said I'm in hospital?
action_responses.request_senior_help: David remains in view while the colleague acknowledges your request.
action_responses.escalate_urgent_concern: The receiving clinician asks you to give a concise structured handover.

fallback_responses: I'm not sure. Could you say that one part at a time?
David looks towards you, then becomes distracted by activity in the corridor.

facts.fact: He is unsure why he is in the room and is looking for his coat.
He can engage briefly when spoken to one question at a time and shown the clock.
He is becoming drowsier and needs his name repeated before responding.
His speech is now limited to one-word replies because his breathing appears more difficult.
